name: Salt marsh
notes: Tidal grassland of salt-tolerant cordgrasses, rushes and succulent glasswort, zoned from the daily-flooded low marsh to a high marsh of salt hay, sea lavender and marsh elder; drawn on the US Atlantic/Gulf coast marshes and NW European (Wadden Sea, UK) saltings.

shrub.name: Marsh elder
shrub.source: Iva frutescens, marsh elder, US Atlantic & Gulf coasts, shrub fringe at the upper edge of salt marsh, 1-3 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Groundsel bush
shrub.source: Baccharis halimifolia, groundsel bush, US Atlantic & Gulf coasts, high salt-marsh border, 1.5-4 m, fluffy white seed heads — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Sea purslane shrub (halimione)
shrub.source: Atriplex portulacoides (Halimione portulacoides), sea purslane, European Atlantic & Mediterranean coasts, grey-leaved shrublet along creek banks of the mid marsh, 30-80 cm — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Cordgrass
ground.source: Spartina (Sporobolus) alterniflora, smooth cordgrass, US Atlantic & Gulf coasts, sole dominant of daily-flooded low marsh, 0.5-2 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Salt hay
ground.source: Spartina (Sporobolus) patens, saltmeadow cordgrass, US Atlantic & Gulf coasts, fine cowlicked sward of the high marsh, 30-80 cm — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Common cordgrass
ground.source: Spartina (Sporobolus) anglica, common cordgrass, NW European estuaries (origin S England), pioneer of intertidal mudflats, 0.3-1.3 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Glasswort
ground.source: Salicornia europaea, common glasswort, coasts of Europe, N America & Asia, succulent annual pioneer of bare intertidal mud, 10-30 cm, reddens in autumn — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Sea lavender
ground.source: Limonium vulgare, common sea lavender, European Atlantic & North Sea coasts, mid-high salt marsh, 20-40 cm, lilac flower sprays in summer — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Black needlerush
ground.source: Juncus roemerianus, black needlerush, US Gulf & S Atlantic coasts, dark stiff stands of the irregularly flooded high marsh, 0.8-1.5 m — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

special.note: Catalogue plants (data/plants) whose band centres fall inside this biome's climate; computed, informational. Phase 6 may raise their density here so they are findable.

associations.name: Cordgrass low marsh
associations.where: creek banks and mudflat edge flooded twice daily, soft mud
associations.source: Spartina alterniflora low marsh (Chapman 1960; Teal 1962; USNVC)

associations.name: Salt hay high marsh
associations.where: flat marsh platform flooded only on spring tides, firm peat
associations.source: Spartina patens high marsh (Niering & Warren 1980; Bertness 1991)

associations.name: Needlerush marsh
associations.where: brackish high marsh and pan margins, irregularly flooded
associations.source: Juncus roemerianus marsh of the Gulf and South Atlantic coasts (Eleuterius 1976; USNVC)

associations.name: Glasswort-sea lavender pioneer marsh
associations.where: open mudflat and salt pans at the lowest marsh edge, bare mud
associations.source: Salicornia pioneer marsh (Rodwell 2000 SM8/SM13; Wadden Sea Beeftink 1977)

associations.name: Halimione-cordgrass European saltmarsh
associations.where: creek levees and upper marsh of NW European saltings, well-drained mud
associations.source: Halimionetum portulacoidis and Spartina anglica marsh (Rodwell 2000 SM6/SM14; Beeftink 1977)
